data.description:
## Context / Problem
GitHub code-scanning alert #88 (`py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization`, Security/quality) flags `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py:51`:

```python
assert "pandoc.org" in text or "github.com/jgm/pandoc" in text, (...)
```

This is not real URL sanitization — there is no untrusted input; the test checks that NOTICE mentions upstream so the GPL source-availability obligation is actionable. But the finding is still worth fixing properly: bare substring matching would accept a NOTICE that only contains a lookalike host such as `evil-pandoc.org.attacker.com` or `notgithub.com/jgm/pandoc`, which does NOT actionably point at upstream. The same rule class was fixed before in `test_llm_fallback_chain.py` (ticket revealable-ungracious-billygoat, alerts 81/82).

## Approach
Replace the two substring checks with a single host-anchored regex assertion that matches the upstream references as proper URLs/hosts:

```python
_UPSTREAM_RE = re.compile(r"https?://(www\.)?pandoc\.org\b|https?://github\.com/jgm/pandoc\b")
assert _UPSTREAM_RE.search(text), (...)
```

The scheme+host anchor means a hostname embedded at an arbitrary position (a lookalike registrable domain) no longer satisfies the assertion, which is exactly what CodeQL's query asks for, while the real NOTICE (which carries full `https://` upstream URLs) still passes. This is the simplest position-aware form; no urlparse machinery is needed because the subject is a whole document, not a single URL. RED-first is satisfied by demonstrating the weakness: show the old expression accepts `notpandoc.org.evil.com` text while the anchored regex rejects it, and that both accept the real NOTICE.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py` — only the upstream-URL assertion in `test_notice_names_pandoc_its_version_and_its_licence`. Do NOT touch the pandoc version pin strings or NOTICE content (a parallel agent is bumping pypandoc-binary in the same file).

Sibling sweep: grep the repo for other substring-`in` checks against URLs/hostnames and check open code-scanning alerts; fix same-file siblings in scope, file discovered_from tickets for anything bigger.

## Testing
This is a test-only change. Verification: `pytest tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py -x -q` stays green against the real NOTICE (happy path); the lookalike-host demonstration above is the failure path showing the anchored form rejects what the old form accepted. `make lint && make typecheck` pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The assertion at `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py:51` no longer uses bare substring containment for `pandoc.org` / `github.com/jgm/pandoc`; it matches scheme+host-anchored upstream references.
- [ ] A NOTICE containing only a lookalike host (e.g. `https://notpandoc.org.evil.com`) does NOT satisfy the new assertion; the real NOTICE does.
- [ ] The test's intent is preserved: NOTICE must actionably point at upstream (pandoc.org or github.com/jgm/pandoc).
- [ ] No version pins or NOTICE content changed; the diff touches only the URL assertion.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` all pass; change pushed to Gerrit.
- [ ] After the fix lands and CodeQL re-runs, alert #88 clears without dismissal.
data.title: code-scanning #88: anchor upstream-URL assertions in NOTICE test (incomplete URL substring sanitization)
